subject: Privileged cycle: communication scenarios, escalation paths, and timeline
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Privileged cycle: communication scenarios, escalation paths, and timeline

Team —

I'm starting a short planning thread to lock down the parts of this year's performance cycle that need special handling (sensitive roles, manager transitions, and limited-visibility calibration). This is intentionally compact — I want to capture scenarios, owners, and where we need vendor or legal support. High-level proposal below. Please reply with +1, a single-line objection, or an edit suggestion.

Summary proposal (draft):
- Timeline: manager self-reviews open 2026-10-05, peer feedback window 2026-10-12 — 10-26, calibration liaisons finalize 2026-11-02, final ratings & comp guidance 2026-11-09.
- Privileged roles: small subset (~15 people) flagged in a restricted folder; communications go on a "quiet path" to avoid leaks. Dedicated CS/HR liaison will manage those.
- Manager transitions: if a manager leaves mid-cycle, use the "manager-transition-checklist.docx" for interim reviewer assignment, brief the interim in private, and extend the peer window by 5 business days.
- Escalation matrix: keep 3 tiers — (1) people ops lead, (2) hiring/HR legal, (3) exec sponsor. I attached a first-draft escalation matrix.
- External moderation: consider bringing Peak HR in to audit calibration for sensitive roles only; Julie is on cc (external) and can propose scope.

Action items (to own):
- Laura: confirm quiet-path comms draft and list of privileged roles (by 2026-09-07).
- Karthik: update calibration rubric to include manager-transition examples (by 2026-09-09).
- Marcus: validate timeline against engraving of comp planning (by 2026-09-08).

Attachments: performance-forms-v2.pdf, escalation-matrix.xlsx, manager-transition-checklist.docx (in the drive link below).

Thanks — short replies appreciated.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of People Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Privileged cycle: communication scenarios, escalation paths, and timeline

Thanks Steph — +1 on the timeline. A couple quick notes: 

1) Quiet-path comms: I'll produce two variants — (A) short legal-safe notice for individuals, (B) manager-facing script for discrete handoffs. I'll list the privileged roles and why they're flagged (sensitivity rationale) to help with audit trails.

2) One scenario we should explicitly add: manager-to-manager handoffs where the new manager is internal but there are active calibration conversations. Suggest adding a hardened step: "freeze ratings for flagged direct reports until liaison confirms handoff."

I'll have a draft comms packet by 2026-09-07 EOD.

— Laura

Director, People Programs | Redwood Inference

Stephanie / Laura —

Couple quick calibration-focused edits:
- Add a manager-transition column to the calibration spreadsheet (example: "Manager left, interim assigned, prior rating locked until liaison signoff").
- For privileged roles, require a second independent reviewer from a different org (peer reviewer) and log the rationale in the restricted drive. That helps for auditability and reduces bias.
- I recommend Peak HR for a limited audit (scope: review 8 privileged role ratings + interview 3 managers). Julie (cc) — can you confirm if this is feasible and ballpark cost?

Action: I'll push a new rubric draft by 2026-09-09 and update the calibration sheet with the manager-transition column.

Thanks for including Peak HR. We can scope a limited audit for privileged roles. Tentative outline and availability:

- Timing: we can do work the week of 2026-10-24 (aligning to your post-peer-window calibration).
- Ballpark: $6k–$9k depending on number of interviews and deliverables.

I'll attach a short questionnaire template for manager interviews and a sample moderation agenda (see attached: peak-questionnaire-template.docx). Happy to join the calibration session remotely.

Best,
